findings.finding: The epic asserts as flat fact that 'all three clients support static bearer; none require OAuth', but rebar's own docs (mcp-auth.md §4) verify ONLY the Claude static-bearer path; the Copilot and Codex HTTP-MCP static-bearer config surfaces (and their exact config-key names, e.g. Codex `bearer_token_env_var`/`http_headers`) are asserted 'research-confirmed' with no citation to those tools' current docs — an unequal evidence class (Claude Verified; Copilot/Codex Partially-verified) for a capability the epic (via olm + jackal) depends on.
findings.location: Epic description 'Exposure/auth' bullet ('all three clients support static bearer; none require OAuth') and child olm's per-client config keys

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the trusted-signing-environment child with parent AC4/ADR decision-3: rewrite it to provision the MCP container to sign under the EXISTING opcert env (same REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + signing key, no new env entry, no gate change), and delete its 'box's own environment id + public key' registration language.
evidence: Parent AC4: '...the MCP container signs under the box's existing opcert env so its op-certs verify against verify.require_environment with no new env/gate change (spoiled-bionic-goose)... a ticket closed via MCP passes verify-opcert against the existing env on main'

ADR child a45f decision 3: 'the MCP server signs them under the box's EXISTING opcert signing environment — the same REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + signing key... There is no new env_id and no change to the single-valued enforcement gate: the box is not a distinct third environment'

b173 AC: '.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml on main contains the box's environment id + its PUBLIC key only'; 'The private signing key is provisioned out-of-band (SSM / secret store)' — i.e. a NEW box key + NEW env entry, not reuse of the existing REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID key
findings.finding: Parent AC4 sub-clause (b) — 'the MCP container signs under the box's EXISTING opcert env so its op-certs verify against verify.require_environment with NO new env/gate change' — is not covered with the same observable outcome by any sibling. The parent decomposition names child 'spoiled-bionic-goose' as this coverer, but the roster contains no goose ticket; the closest sibling, b173-e50a-4b93-455f, instead registers the box as a DISTINCT trusted signing environment with the box's OWN environment id + its OWN public key ('.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml on main contains the box's environment id + its PUBLIC key only'; 'a cert signed by the box's key VERIFIES'). That is the distinct-third-env model the parent + ADR child a45f decision-3 EXPLICITLY REJECTED (Option A: 'no new env_id and no change to the enforcement gate'; 'the box is not a distinct third environment').
findings.location: child b173-e50a-4b93-455f (and parent AC4 sub-part b)
scenarios: Completion verifier runs `verify-opcert` on a ticket closed via MCP: parent expects the cert to verify against the EXISTING env id already named by the single-valued verify.require_environment; b173 produces a cert signed by a NEW box key requiring a NEW env entry, which cannot be named by a single-valued gate without the gate change the ADR forbids.
Container coverage audit at epic close: AC4(b)'s stated checked-oracle (verify against the existing env, no new env/gate change) is never asserted by any child; b173 asserts the opposite (a new env).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace b173's acceptance oracle with: 'The MCP container is configured to sign under the existing REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID and the existing signing key; a plan-review/completion cert minted via MCP VERIFIES against the single-valued verify.require_environment naming the EXISTING env, with no new entry added to .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml and no change to the enforcement gate; an otherwise-identical cert from an unregistered env is rejected.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the trusted-env child's name and design consistent with the parent decomposition (spoiled-bionic-goose = sign under the EXISTING env) and update starling's dependency wording so 'the box is a registered trusted signing environment' is replaced with 'the box signs under the existing opcert env' to match the ADR.
evidence: Parent decomposition item 5: 'spoiled-bionic-goose — provision the MCP container to sign under the box's EXISTING opcert env (same signing key + REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID)...'

aa0b: 'Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR decides routing/auth), and the trusted-env registration slice (guidance claims certified ops are enforceable via MCP, which is only true once the box is a trusted env).'

aa0b scope-2: 'enforceable because the box is a registered trusted signing environment (the trusted-env slice)' — implies the box IS a distinct registered env, matching b173 but contradicting the ADR's 'box is not a distinct third environment'
b173: 'Blocks: inadequate-hydrated-starling (guidance asserts certified ops are enforceable via MCP, true only once the box is a trusted env).'
findings.finding: Dependency/roster-reference gap: multiple children name a sibling ('spoiled-bionic-goose') that does not appear in the sibling roster, while the roster's b173 (which appears to substitute for it) embodies a contradictory design. Child aa0b (starling) declares 'Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR), and the trusted-env registration slice' and its scope says 'enforceable because the box is a registered trusted signing environment (the trusted-env slice)'; the parent decomposition and AC4 both name 'spoiled-bionic-goose' with the EXISTING-env framing. b173 self-describes as registering the box as a NEW trusted signing environment. The referenced dependency target is therefore ambiguous/inconsistent across parent and children.
scenarios: Plan-review of starling: it must document certified-op routing consistent with its blocker. If the blocker (b173) registers a new box env, starling's docs will assert a distinct trusted env; but the ADR (mosasaur/a45f) it also depends on says the box is NOT a distinct env — starling receives two contradictory design inputs.
Coverage audit: the child named by the parent (goose) is absent; the substitute (b173) carries the rejected design, so the dependency chain rests on an inconsistent node.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename/rescope b173 to match the parent's 'spoiled-bionic-goose' (provision MCP to sign under the existing opcert env, no new env) and revise aa0b's scope-2 + dependency text to drop the 'registered [new] trusted signing environment' framing in favor of 'signs under the existing REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID env'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml conflict: pick the ADR's existing-env model (no new entry, no gate change) and rewrite the trusted-env child's rollback/oracle to not depend on a newly added box env entry.
evidence: b173 Compat: 'Rollback = remove the box's entry from .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml (MCP-minted certs then stop verifying; existing paths unaffected).'
a45f decision 3: 'the same REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + signing key already pinned in .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml on main... no new env_id and no change to the single-valued enforcement gate'
Parent design summary: 'those certs are enforceable with NO new env_id and NO change to the enforcement gate (ADR 0049's single-env model is preserved; the box is not a distinct third env)'
findings.finding: Conflicting-assumptions mode between the trusted-env child (b173) and the ADR child (a45f) about whether verify.require_environment or trusted_environments.yaml changes. a45f decision-3 asserts 'NO change to the single-valued enforcement gate' and no new env entry; b173's compat note says 'Rollback = remove the box's entry from .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml (MCP-minted certs then stop verifying)', which presupposes a NEW entry was ADDED to that authoritative file — a change a45f's design forecloses.
scenarios: Landing b173 adds a new environment entry to .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml; landing a45f asserts no such entry is added. The two lands cannot both be truthful about the authoritative trust file.
verify-opcert enforcement: a single-valued verify.require_environment can name only one env; b173 adds a second, forcing the gate change a45f says never happens.
findings.suggested_fix: Change b173 so it commits NO new entry to .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml (the existing opcert env entry already suffices) and its rollback is 'revert the MCP container's signing-env provisioning'; align its verify oracle with the single existing env.
